label: Browser (BabylonJS), direct to player
description: A browser game built on BabylonJS, hosted on your own site and sold directly to players without a storefront or app store.

items.description: Static hosting and CDN chosen (e.g. Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, S3 + CloudFront), with HTTPS and a custom domain; WebGL, audio and storage APIs need a secure context
Initial download budget set (e.g. under 20 MB before first playable frame) and measured on a throttled connection; players bounce from a long first load
Brotli or gzip compression configured for JS, WASM and JSON, with correct Content-Type and Content-Encoding headers; misconfigured WASM MIME types break streaming compile
Asset versioning and cache headers decided (hashed filenames, long max-age, short-lived index.html) so updates reach players without stale-cache bugs
Loading screen with real progress shown while assets stream in, and a visible error state if loading fails
Supported browser matrix written down (Chrome, Firefox, Safari desktop, Safari iOS, Chrome Android) with minimum versions, and an unsupported-browser message
Render backend decided: WebGL2 baseline, WebGPU optional; fallback behavior defined when a device lacks WebGPU or has a blocklisted GPU
Audio unlock on first user gesture handled; browsers block autoplay audio until the player interacts
Input methods defined: keyboard and mouse, gamepad (Gamepad API), and touch if mobile browsers are in scope
Fullscreen, pointer lock, tab-hidden pause and window resize behavior defined and tested
BabylonJS version pinned, with a plan for engine upgrades mid-project
Asset pipeline formats fixed: glTF/GLB for models, KTX2/Basis for textures, Draco or meshopt compression; exporter and settings documented
Performance budget set on a named low-end target device: frame rate, draw calls, texture memory, JS heap
Build and bundling set up (e.g. Vite) with tree-shaken Babylon imports and a reproducible production build command
Save storage chosen (localStorage, IndexedDB, or server-side accounts) with its size limits understood
Browser storage eviction handled: Safari can clear script-writable storage after days without a visit, and private browsing may not persist at all; players are warned or saves are backed up
Save format versioned with a migration path so updates do not corrupt existing saves
Save export and import (or cloud save) offered so players can move between browsers and devices
Checkout provider chosen (e.g. Stripe, Paddle, Lemon Squeezy); a merchant of record handles VAT and sales tax for you
Purchase entitlement defined: how a paying player unlocks the game (account login, license key, signed token) and how it survives a cleared browser
Free demo vs paid content boundary defined, and enforced server-side if piracy matters
Refund policy and support contact published; payment providers require one
Privacy policy, terms of sale and cookie consent in place for analytics and payments (GDPR, CCPA)
Landing page with trailer or GIF, screenshots, price and a play button above the fold
Open Graph and Twitter card metadata set so shared links show an image and title
Privacy-respecting analytics for funnel steps: page view, load complete, first play, purchase
Client error reporting (e.g. Sentry) with WebGL context-lost and out-of-memory errors captured
